t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup in Swiss International Typographic Style. Small grey eyebrow and a large light-weight navy sans headline at top left. Below, a 3 by 2 grid of square-cornered tiles with even gutters, alternating deep navy and limestone. Text tiles carry a huge numeral with a slash, a hairline rule, a regular sans title and a short note for <CONTENT>. One tile holds a pale-blue blueprint line drawing of a skid on navy; one is an abstract composition of flat limestone, navy and steel-blue planes. Flat, no shadows.
signature_idea: System links as a Swiss checkerboard of slash-numbered tiles, closed by a blueprint tile and one abstract steel-blue plane.
strengths: very close to the brand: navy/limestone, light headline, square corners
slash numerals give a strong, scannable order
blueprint tile adds equipment context without clutter
maps cleanly to an existing tile-grid component
weaknesses: abstract steel-blue tile means nothing and reads as filler
numerals are heavier than the light headline
tiles show no link affordance (no arrow or action)
notes repeat endotoxin claims and a PP temperature figure that look factual
white page ground instead of limestone
brand_fit_why: Navy and limestone tiles, a single steel-blue plane, light headline, slash numerals and square corners match the brand book almost exactly.
